turns.content: For triangle ABC, we know BC = 12 and ∠B = 30°; let AC = b and AB = c. Which side is opposite the known angle, and which quantities are fixed?
Apply the Law of Sines to derive a linear equation for c, and use that equation to find when there are two distinct real values of c.
Use the sum and product of the roots of the quadratic obtained by taking AC=12 as its constant-side input, and determine when both possible values of c are positive.
Check whether either boundary value gives two distinct positive lengths.
List the admissible integer values of b.
Count the integer values of AC, including both boundary values, for which two values of AB are possible.
